text: Better a dry crust with quietthan a house full of feasting with strife. [1]
A wise servant will rule over an unworthy son,and will share the inheritance of the children. [2]
The crucible for silver, and the furnace for gold,but the tester of hearts is the Lord.
The evildoer gives heed to wicked lips,the liar, to a mischievous tongue.
Whoever mocks the poor reviles their Maker;whoever rejoices in their misfortune will not go unpunished. [AA]
Children's children are the crown of the elderly,and the glory of children is their parentage.
Fine words ill fit a fool;how much more lying lips, a noble!
A bribe seems a charm to its user;at every turn it brings success. [3]
Whoever overlooks an offense fosters friendship,but whoever gossips about it separates friends. [4]
A single reprimand does more for a discerning personthan a hundred lashes for a fool. [5]
The wicked pursue only rebellion,and a merciless messenger is sent against them. [6]
Face a bear robbed of her cubs,but never fools in their folly! [7]
If you return evil for good,evil will not depart from your house. [8] [AB]
The start of strife is like the opening of a dam;check a quarrel before it bursts forth!
Whoever acquits the wicked, [AC] whoever condemns the just—both are an abomination to the Lord.
Of what use is money in the hands of foolswhen they have no heart to acquire wisdom? [9]
A friend is a friend at all times,and a brother is born for the time of adversity. [AD]
Those without sense give their hands in pledge,becoming surety for their neighbors. [AE]
Those who love an offense love a fight; [AF]those who build their gate high [10] court disaster.
The perverse in heart come to no good,and the double-tongued fall into trouble. [11]
Whoever conceives a fool has grief;the father of a numskull has no joy.
A joyful heart is the health of the body,but a depressed spirit dries up the bones. [AG]
A guilty person takes out a bribe from the pocket,thus perverting the course of justice. [12]
On the countenance of a discerning person is wisdom, [AH]but the eyes of a fool are on the ends of the earth. [13]
A foolish son is vexation to his father,and bitter sorrow to her who bore him. [AI]
It is wrong to fine an innocent person,but beyond reason to scourge nobles.
Those who spare their words are truly knowledgeable,and those who are discreet are intelligent. [AJ]
Even fools, keeping silent, are considered wise;if they keep their lips closed, intelligent. [14]
